scope: Read-only source inventory for receive packet ZC_AUTORUN_SKILL (0x0147), temporary skill storage, and its message-126 call.

primary_source.detail: Receive dispatcher case 327 (0x0147) calls CGameMode::Zc_autorun_skill(this, buf), then exits the dispatch branch.

Zc_autorun_skill creates SKILL_INFO, sets m_isValid=1, populates fields from the raw packet, resolves the skill ID name, calls CSession::AddTempSkillItem, then calls SendMsg with messageId=126, val1=&skillInfo, val2=skillInfo.level, val3=0. Decompiled spelling is this->CMode::SendMsg; the selected PE confirms this call dispatches virtually through vtable slot offset 0x14 at VA 0x5A1205.

The selected call reaches virtual CGameMode::SendMsg at 0x5833a0; switch case 0x7e is decimal message 126. It treats packed 64-bit val1 as low-DWORD pointer to SKILL_INFO and high-DWORD level, then switches on descriptor type at pointer+8: 1 sends message 79 with selector 2; 2 sends 79 with selector 1; 4 selects recipient GID by SKID family, sends message 76 with SKID/GID/level, then sends 79 with zero arguments; 8, 0x10, and 0x20 send message 79 with selectors 3, 4, and 5; other values return SUT_NOSKILL.

The base CMode::SendMsg implementation handles message 2 and 75 only and otherwise returns 0. It is not the selected recipient for the autorun message-126 call according to the PE virtual-call evidence.
AddTempSkillItem appends a new skill snapshot. On duplicate SKID, only level, SKID, spcost, and upgradable are updated; the rest of the existing row is preserved.
GetTempSkillItemInfoBySkillId searches the temporary list by SKID and returns the first match or null; the list is distinct from regular player, homunculus, and mercenary skill lists.

port_mapping.detail: HandleAutoRunSkill is registered for 0x0147. It rejects null data, wrong packet id, length other than 39, or bytes 0-1 other than 47 01. It reads SKID at +2, type +4, signed level/spcost/range at +8/+10/+12, upgradable +38; sets m_isValid=1; applies metadata and copies skillIdName to skillName; inserts through g_session.AddTemporarySkillItem.

Temporary list and Add/Get/Clear APIs are separate from the normal, guild, homun, and merc skill collections. Duplicate insertion preserves prior metadata and changes only level/SKID/spcost/upgradable.
When normal player-skill lookup misses or returns an invalid row, the port falls back to GetTemporarySkillItemBySkillId for skill selection.

Port CGameMode::SendMsg has no case 126 branch, and HandleAutoRunSkill does not translate the raw skill type into source selector-79/76 dispatches. Its MC_IDENTIFY branch instead sends SendIdentifySkillUseRequest directly.
Port does not issue a generic message-126 SendMsg call. It calls SendIdentifySkillUseRequest only when SKID equals kSkillMerchantIdentify; other auto-run skill rows only populate temporary storage.
CGameMode::SendMsg has no case 126 in its message switch. Current 0x0147 handler does not route its parsed row or raw arguments into that switch.

parity_observations: The packet field offsets, 39-byte framing, temporary-row insertion, and duplicate-row update policy are represented in the port handler/session APIs.

The source call arguments are a pointer to stack-local SKILL_INFO, its level, and zero. The selected PE confirms virtual dispatch to CGameMode::SendMsg, where case 0x7e/126 dispatches by SKILL_INFO.type.
The port currently lacks a general message-126 selector dispatch. Its MC_IDENTIFY direct-send path is not equivalent to source type-4 behavior unless recipient and sequencing are proven equivalent.
unresolved_questions: For type 4, do the port's canonical companion IDs and all supported SKID families reproduce source recipient selection?
Should the port's MC_IDENTIFY special-case remain attached to 0x0147 handling or be replaced by source type-specific dispatch? Root owns this parity decision.
root_review: Inventory describes baseline before integration. Root verified source and selected PE; authoritative decisions/current gates: PK27-autorun-source-review.json.
